chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Muhammad al-Ansari, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The believer adheres to the discipline of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When He expands [his provision], he expands, and when He withholds [from him], he withholds.'
ai.seo_question: How should a believer respond to changes in their financial provision according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes 'adab Allah' (the etiquette of God) as the moral compass for a believer’s response to divine decree, linking material provision to spiritual comportment. It teaches that just as Allah expands or restricts sustenance, the believer must mirror this dynamic by expanding generosity when blessed and exercising restraint when tested, reflecting a state of constant gratitude and patience.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Muhammad Al Ansary, fro Umar Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Believer takes by the disciplining of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. Whenever He<sup>azwj</sup> Expands upon him, he expands, and when He<sup>azwj</sup> Withholds upon him, he withholds’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali has narrated from Muhammad ibn Bandar from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu Muhammad al- Ansariy from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘The believing person follows the discipline of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious. When Allah grants him extended favors, he becomes generous; and when He holds back, he also spares his means.’”
